36 complete natural lives

2581 decisions; 596 revised-story encounters across 40 different revised situations. Every life completed. No five-year cooldown violation, missing nonfatal result or unresolved binding token.

These are actual commands, results and journals from the engine lifetime tests at 42edd00. The strategy always takes the first available choice; it does not manually create careers, relationships or hobbies. Focused tests exercise every revised alternative and its required domain context.

Age 1 · first-bubble-catch

A very brief possession

A soap bubble floats past your nose. You reach for it. Your new favourite thing has already resigned.

  • Go after the next one — chosen
  • Watch where it goes
  • Complain about the disappearing bubble

Plenty of vacancies

There are more bubbles. You spend several happy minutes failing to keep any of them.

  • Happiness: +4%
  • Energy: -2%

I chased soap bubbles and caught absolutely nothing.

Age 3 · shoe-principle

A principled disagreement

Ruby says shoes are necessary for going outside. You were not consulted during the drafting of this policy.

  • Let Ruby help — chosen
  • Insist on doing it yourself

Terms accepted

Both shoes make it onto the correct feet. A surprisingly productive morning.

  • Ruby Kelly · relationship: +3%

I let Ruby help with my shoes.

To dodge chores, you left a dummy in your dressing gown at your desk. Alice is now giving it a serious talk about responsibility. The dummy is handling it well.

  • Step out and take over the discussion — chosen
  • Leave a second dummy to play Alice
  • Stay hidden and let the dummy handle it

A noticeable improvement in posture

Alice says the dummy already agreed to take the rubbish out. You do it while the dummy remains at the desk, apparently thinking about its future.

  • Discipline: +3%
  • Energy: -2%
  • Alice Ricci · relationship: +0%

I replaced a dummy during Alice’s lecture and did the chore it had agreed to.

Age 18 · adult-queue-merge · revised

The accidental millionaire

At a charity auction, someone mistakes you for a wealthy donor. The auctioneer hands you the microphone beside a photograph of an elderly donkey. “How much will you give?” The room goes quiet.

  • Admit your wealth has been exaggerated — chosen
  • Donate €233.14 to the donkey charity
  • Claim you are the donkey’s lawyer

A donkey-sized misunderstanding

You explain that you were looking for the toilets. The auctioneer takes back the microphone and points down the corridor. Several people applaud your honesty. One applauds the donkey.

  • Respect: +4%
  • Stress: +0%

I admitted I was not the wealthy donor a charity auction expected.

Age 19 · adult-repair-table

Nothing to worry about

At a free repair demonstration, a wind-up toy starts smoking. The volunteer explains that it is supposed to do that. The label “DO NOT WIND” drops off its base.

  • Ask what the label means — chosen
  • Step back and let them stop it
  • Ask whether smoke costs extra

A useful admission

The volunteer stops and explains the failed mechanism. You learn more from the mistake than from the planned demonstration.

  • Smarts: +4%
  • Respect: +1%

I asked about a warning label during a failed toy-repair demonstration.

Age 1 · first-nap-negotiation

Too busy to be tired

Test extended

Age 2 · first-echo

Encore! Encore!

You bang a spoon on a bowl. It makes a brilliant noise. You would like to check that result another twenty times.

  • Give the full concert — chosen
  • Try a different rhythm
  • Look inside the bowl

A short, loud career

Age 50 · adult-neighbourhood-song · revised

The song of extra garlic

At a community singalong, the lyric projector fails. It starts displaying a takeaway receipt instead. The backing track continues. Everyone looks to you for the first line.

  • Sing the receipt with feeling — chosen
  • Pass the microphone down the row
  • Demand that they restore the proper words

Hold the onions

You hit the high note on “extra garlic”. The room joins in for “delivery instructions”. The organiser finally switches off the projector during the sauce options.

  • Happiness: +7%
  • Energy: -3%

I led a singalong using a takeaway receipt as the lyrics.

Age 52 · familiar-street · revised

A very local tragedy

On a free history walk in Melbourne, the guide points at a laundrette: “A forbidden romance began here.” The owner leans out and asks whether this is about the washing-machine warranty.

  • Stay for both versions — chosen
  • Ask the owner for the real story
  • Leave before the historical reenactment

Star-crossed and spin-dried

The guide describes a doomed affair. The owner describes a parts supplier. You finish the walk unsure which relationship suffered more.

  • Happiness: +4%
  • Fitness: +2%

I heard two competing tragedies outside a laundrette in Melbourne.

Age 55 · adult-lost-glove · revised

The lost hand

You pick up a glove from a bench. A rubber hand slides out of its sleeve. It has painted fingernails, a wristwatch and no obvious owner.

  • Carry it to reception — chosen
  • Leave it upright on the bench
  • Ask around for anyone missing a hand

Please wave if this is yours

The receptionist holds the hand above the counter. A magician hurries over, thanks you and immediately removes its thumb. You stop watching.

  • Respect: +3%
  • Stress: -2%

I returned a magician’s rubber hand to reception.

Age 56 · adult-community-poster

The missing letter

A poster for a free public cookery class has dropped the L from “public”. The organiser cannot work out why people keep arriving with suspicious questions.

  • Point out the missing letter quietly — chosen
  • Leave the organiser to discover it
  • Read the heading aloud to the queue

A little tape saves the afternoon

The organiser repairs the heading and looks at the queue with fresh concern. The class returns to soup.

  • Respect: +3%
  • Discipline: +2%

I pointed out an embarrassing typo on a cookery-class poster.

You sit in the last free café chair. A child wearing an enormous tie tells you it is reserved for an important businessman. The businessman, they explain, is them.

  • Explain that reserving chairs is bad business

A volatile juice market

  • Happiness: +5%
  • Stress: -2%

  • Stress: -2%

Age 63 · adult-instruction-last-page · revised

Not the tabletop version

At a craft workshop, you pull the tab on a kit labelled “decorative boat”. A full-size inflatable canoe starts filling the room. The tiny instruction sheet says to inflate outdoors.

  • Deflate it before it reaches the doorway — chosen
  • Climb in and ask for paddles
  • Insist the picture on the box was misleading

A long public fart

You open the valve. The canoe collapses over eight uninterrupted seconds of rude noise. The instructor waits until everyone has stopped laughing to explain the warning.

  • Discipline: +4%
  • Energy: -4%

I deflated a full-size canoe during a crowded craft workshop.

  • Give it a terrible score for poor eye contact

A quiet, grounded child

  • Respect: +2%
  • Energy: -3%

I praised a bonnet-wearing cabbage at a vegetable baby contest.

At a community singalong, the lyric projector fails. It starts displaying a takeaway receipt instead. The backing track continues. Everyone looks to you for the first line.

  • Pass the microphone down the row
  • Demand that they restore the proper words

Hold the onions

You hit the high note on “extra garlic”. The room joins in for “delivery instructions”. The organiser finally switches off the projector during the sauce options.

  • Happiness: +0%
  • Energy: -3%

I led a singalong using a takeaway receipt as the lyrics.

Age 21 · adult-weather-expert · revised

The door does not believe in you

An automatic shop door refuses to open for you. It opens for a child, a trolley and a blowing receipt. You step forward. Nothing. The cashier points at the sensor and suggests waving.

  • Ask the cashier to let you out — chosen
  • Follow the trolley out
  • Perform an increasingly furious dance

Assisted departure

The cashier walks over. The doors open immediately for them. They hold the sensor while you leave, like a bouncer escorting out a ghost.

  • Stress: +0%

I had to ask a cashier to release me through an automatic door.

A successful cancellation
